heading: Mind
games
playground.intro: I study how attention and memory work, and I design around their limits. Try them on yourself. Each one takes under a minute.

games.name: Say the color
games.rule: Pick the color of the ink. Ignore what the word says.
games.lesson: Reading is automatic, so it gets in the way. This is why a screen should never make two signals disagree.

games.name: Hold that number
games.rule: Watch the digits, then type them back. It gets longer each round.
games.lesson: Working memory is small. Most adults hold about seven digits, which is why I give each screen one decision.

games.name: Quick draw
games.rule: Wait for green, then click as fast as you can. Five tries.
games.lesson: A quarter of a second is typical. Feedback that arrives slower than that starts to feel broken.
